observed_bottleneck: Parent n-6174d6127af5 always publishes the fifth and final pretraining epoch after only one terminal 256-draw support check and a permissive unique-valid-rate threshold of 0.01, so it cannot reject a late checkpoint whose corpus likelihood improved while its ancestral chemical support worsened. That missing selection step matters because the three independently prepared Parent artifacts show seed-sensitive support: prior unique-valid rate ranges from 0.8125 to 0.85546875, online complete-conditioned novel-valid yield ranges from 0.7832720190434971 to 0.8541171385346877, vocabulary size ranges from 74 to 78, and seed-level macro score ranges from 0.498752613558053 to 0.544472616912355. These paired variations do not prove that the terminal checkpoint caused the score spread, but they identify blind final-epoch publication as the active-layer behavior that leaves the weakest prepared artifact unprotected.
hypothesis: Replace blind terminal-epoch publication with label-free ancestral-support checkpoint selection inside the unchanged five-epoch corpus pretraining run: retain the epoch whose fixed preparation-only probe produces the highest unique-valid fraction, and publish that epoch's model state as the frozen prior.
method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb autoregressive SMILES policy optimization
method_thesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES language model on the allowed unlabeled corpus and freeze a copy as the molecular prior. During each objective session, sample complete molecules de novo token by token from a trainable agent, rank the accepted molecules by their observed oracle rewards, and update the agent only on the highest-reward fraction using the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: the squared gap between agent log-likelihood and a target formed from prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward. Excluding low-reward samples from policy updates prevents them from repeatedly pulling the agent back toward the prior, while prior likelihood still regularizes the elite updates; this concentrates the scarce feedback on sequences associated with improvement of final Top-1 without screening a finite molecular pool.
